description: User-requested Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan-associated research leads. Both are deliberately classified as pending-review practice records because available evidence does not establish actual OA use.

records.title: Run Length Encoding
records.assessmentType: Goldman Sachs candidate-reported interview question (not OA-confirmed)
records.evidenceNote: A public Goldman Sachs interview experience for a 2+ years experienced Software Engineer reports Run-length encoding in a CoderPad interview round, not the online assessment. The GeeksforGeeks practice page also lists Goldman Sachs among company tags. This is retained as an employer-associated practice reference, not a verified OA. It overlaps conceptually with String Compression in the DSA curriculum. Interview report: https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/interview-experiences/goldman-sachs-interview-experience-for-software-engineer-2-yrs-experienced-september-2020/
records.statement: Given a string, encode consecutive runs of the same character by writing the character followed by the number of consecutive occurrences. For example, aaaabbbccc becomes a4b3c3.

records.title: Maximize Count of Increasing Pairs
records.assessmentType: JPMorgan Chase unverified company association (research lead; not OA-confirmed)
records.evidenceNote: The canonical GeeksforGeeks problem is available, but the company attribution as a JPMorgan OA could not be independently corroborated in the sources checked. Included at the user's request as a pending research lead only; do not treat this as proof of a JPMorgan assessment.
records.statement: Given two arrays a1 and a2, maximize the number of disjoint pairs (i, j) such that 2 * a1[i] <= a2[j]. Each element may be used in at most one pair.
